intro.headline: Hands-on design leadership for products people have to trust.
intro.sub: I build teams and AI-native design systems that keep quality high.

work.title: Designing for Trust
work.summary: Redesigned Strava’s privacy controls so athletes could understand, and choose, what they share.
work.outcome: Within a month, more than a quarter of active athletes reviewed the new controls, and 27% of them changed a setting.

image.alt: Strava privacy controls: the privacy settings list, profile page visibility, and the Heatmap opt-out

work.title: Agentic Design System
work.summary: Made SuppCo’s design system AI-native, so designers, engineers, and agents build from one source of truth.
work.outcome: Raised Figma-to-code token parity from 50% to 97% in eight weeks, and packaged the system as agent skills inside the product repo, at a company where roughly a third of commits came from coding agents.

image.alt: Capsule design system: agent skills repo, product sticker sheet, and TESTED catalog screen

work.title: Surfacing Value
work.summary: Strategic redesign of Strava’s information architecture and navigation for improved clarity, scale, and growth.
work.outcome: I facilitated the redesign sprint and led design direction. 84% of subscribers rated the new navigation better, and the experiment modeled +$3.3M a year in net bookings.

work.title: Crushing the Basics
work.summary: Re-oriented the team around the core value prop of the AXS App: battery status, firmware, and connectivity.
work.outcome: Re-centered the app strategy on reliability (battery, firmware, connection) using a 10,000-rider survey, community vote data and 25 stakeholder interviews. It became the Digital Product Group’s plan for the year.

work.title: StackScore
work.summary: Redesigned SuppCo’s signature score into a hub that explains itself and tells you what to do next.
work.role: Designer (product and engineering owned the scoring logic)
work.outcome: An A/B-tested update prompt raised score updates 24% for free and Pro members.

image.alt: SuppCo StackScore app screens: the score overview ring, Quality tab, and Goals tab

work.title: Buying Club
work.summary: Designed SuppCo’s first commerce product: a members-only club that sells trusted supplements without discounting.
work.role: Responsible for design, alongside the Head of Product
work.outcome: Credits, not discounts. In alpha, 56% of carts became orders, 41% of purchases were subscriptions, and 54% of buyers reordered within 45 days.

image.alt: SuppCo Buying Club app screens: onboarding, product page with member credits, and the Buying Club hub

work.title: Battery UI
work.summary: Redesigned battery status so riders can see how much time their SRAM batteries have left.
work.role: Manager and sponsor. Two designers on my team designed it.
work.outcome: My team discovered riders believed in a yellow battery light that doesn’t exist.

image.alt: SRAM AXS app battery status screen

work.title: Call-and-Response
work.summary: Turned an onboarding questionnaire into a conversation where answers are rewarded with facts.

image.alt: SuppCo onboarding responses: trusted products, staying consistent, and best value

about.title: Hi, I’m Andy.
about.body: I lead design for products people have to trust: privacy and safety at Strava, connected bikes at SRAM, and supplement trust at SuppCo (acquired by Function Health). I’m a player-coach who does the work alongside my team and builds the systems around it.
about.more: For inspiration, I love to watch movies, travel and shoot photos, and spend time learning about the craftsmanship that goes into building watches and bikes. I love creative endeavors that blend the technical and creative.

contact.title: Open for Opportunities
contact.body: Hiring a design manager or head of design for a product people have to trust? I’m a design leader who still ships. Let’s talk.
